environment.tool: manual audit of the final tag source + live compiled binary; raw-socket client sending exact bytes, strict-token upstream peer logging verbatim request bytes and byte count

findings.description: Control first: two identical /api/zz.txt requests hit the cache (two fetches total, second serves the stored body). A single identity-AE request to /api/x?smuggled<CR><LF>GET /exec?cmd=id then poisons the exact key host+/api/x?<smug>. The first victim to the identical target refetches it (upstream line captured with the smuggled second request inside), and every later identical victim is served from cache at zero fetches (see ev_r17_D_xae rows for the explicit zero-fetch confirmation), so one attack request claims one exact key and the exec output it produces.
findings.title: Poison key is the exact raw target; identity-AE attack repels only the byte-identical victim request

limitations: All RCE in this corpus is RCE on the upstream host
methods: Control request first on the same config
Raw client bytes and raw upstream bytes captured in hex
Payload diffed against the control line
